findings.issue_text: [Medium/security] app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 — `should_block?` uses an exact, case-sensitive `where(email: email)` match with no normalization (downcasing/stripping) of either the submitted email or stored blocked emails; on PostgreSQL, submitting `Bad@Spam.com` when `bad@spam.com` is blocked completely bypasses the block, while the domain blacklist regex in the same validator is case-insensitive — inconsistent and trivially circumventable

[Medium/bug] app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16 — `should_block?` performs a DB write (`record.save`) inside `User` validation, so nominally read-only checks like `user.valid?`/`save` mutate `blocked_emails`; repeated validations of the same record (e.g., a `valid?` precheck followed by `save`, or retry loops) double-increment `match_count` and rewrite `last_match_at`, and any failure of the inner save (DB error, unique violation) raises an exception out of the validation path instead of producing a normal validation failure

[Low/concurrency] app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16 — `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email lose counter increments (last writer wins); should use an atomic update such as `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")`

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274-276 — the client adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever the response contains any `errors.email`, not just blocked-email errors; e.g., "has already been taken" or whitelist "not allowed" failures also permanently flag the address, after which the inline tip shows the generic `user.email.invalid` message, misreporting the actual problem for that email

[Low/data] db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5 — `action_type` is declared `null: false` with no column default; the default is only applied by a `before_validation` callback, so any insert bypassing model validations (manual/SQL loads of the table, `save(validate: false)`, bulk imports) will fail or store NULL; the default should be set at the DB level in the migration

[Medium/test_gap] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — the new spec only exercises the blocked-email branch (with `should_block?` stubbed) by calling `validate_each` directly; the whitelist and blacklist branches of the moved code, and the end-to-end wiring on `User` (`validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`), have no coverage — a miswired `if:` condition or broken validator resolution would not be caught

[Low/test_gap] app/controllers/users_controller.rb:197-199 — the new `errors`/`values` JSON keys form an untested server↔client contract that create_account_controller.js depends on (`result.errors.email`, `result.values.email`); no controller spec verifies the serialized shape (e.g., that symbol keys from `errors.to_hash` arrive as strings in JSON, and that `values.email` is present whenever `errors.email` is), so a serialization change would silently break the client-side rejection feature

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16 — `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email lose counter increments (last writer wins); should use an atomic update such as `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")`

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, the code does `record.match_count += 1` and `record.last_match_at = Time.zone.now` followed by `record.save` after fetching the row (`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`). This is a non-atomic read/modify/write sequence; concurrent calls for the same `blocked_emails` row can overwrite each other and lose `match_count` increments (and potentially clobber `last_match_at`), i.e., last-writer-wins. The diff clearly introduces this update pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274-276 — the client adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever the response contains any `errors.email`, not just blocked-email errors; e.g., "has already been taken" or whitelist "not allowed" failures also permanently flag the address, after which the inline tip shows the generic `user.email.invalid` message, misreporting the actual problem for that email

adjudication.rationale: In create_account_controller.js, on failed account creation the client does `if (result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values) { rejectedEmails.pushObject(result.values.email); }` (around lines 271-276). This triggers for any server-side `errors.email` (e.g., uniqueness, whitelist/blacklist, blocked), not specifically blocked emails. Later, `emailValidation` immediately fails if `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` and returns reason `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, overriding the actual error reason and causing the inline tip to show a generic “invalid” message for an address that may be valid but already taken/not_allowed/etc. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff (rejectedEmails + contains check + pushObject on any email error).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5 — `action_type` is declared `null: false` with no column default; the default is only applied by a `before_validation` callback, so any insert bypassing model validations (manual/SQL loads of the table, `save(validate: false)`, bulk imports) will fail or store NULL; the default should be set at the DB level in the migration

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `blocked_emails.action_type` as `null: false` without a DB-level default, while the model sets a default only via `before_validation :set_defaults`. This means inserts that bypass validations/callbacks (e.g., direct SQL loads or `save(validate: false)` which skips `before_validation`) can hit a NOT NULL violation. The finding’s “store NULL” phrasing is slightly off (DB would reject NULL), but the schema/robustness concern is real and grounded in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves the domain whitelist/blacklist logic from `User#email_validator` into the new `EmailValidator#validate_each` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb), and changes `User` to use `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`. The added spec `spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb` only exercises the blocked-email path by stubbing `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and calling `validate_each` directly; it does not cover the whitelist/blacklist branches in `EmailValidator`, nor does it verify the end-to-end wiring that the custom validator is actually invoked via the `User` model validation. This is a concrete coverage gap for newly introduced/moved logic, even if not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new server→client response shape in `UsersController#create` (`errors: user.errors.to_hash`, `values: user.attributes.slice(...)`) and the client now conditionally depends on `result.errors.email` and `result.values.email` to push into `rejectedEmails` (create_account_controller.js). The added specs cover `EmailValidator`/`BlockedEmail` behavior, but there’s no test in the diff that exercises the controller JSON serialization/shape, so the contract could regress (e.g., key names/availability) without failing tests. This is a concrete test gap tied to the new feature, not a proven runtime bug.
